steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step.

**Given information:**
- Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026
- Submissions close in six days on Friday at 11:59 PM PT
- I need to convert to Madrid time (CET/CEST)

**Finding the deadline date:**
Six days from Saturday, October 24, 2026 is Friday, October 30, 2026.

**Time zone conversion:**
- Deadline: Friday, October 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time)
- In late October, PT is PDT (UTC-7)
- Madrid is in CET (UTC+1) in late October
- Time difference: CET is 8 hours ahead of PDT

**Converting the time:**
11:59 PM PDT on October 30 = 11:59 + 8 hours = 7:59 AM CET on October 31

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to figure out when "this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time" is in Madrid time.

Starting from Friday, October 30, 2026:
- "This coming Monday" = Monday, November 2, 2026
- Time: 10:00 AM Los Angeles time

Time zone conversion:
- Los Angeles is in PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) in late October/early November, which is UTC-7
- Madrid is in CET (Central European Time) in early November, which is UTC+1
- The difference is 8 hours (Madrid is 8 hours ahead)

So 10:00 AM PDT on Monday, November 2, 2026:
- 10:00 AM + 8 hours = 6:00 PM (18:00)
- Same day: Monday, November 2, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Hackathon End Time Calculation

Given information:
- Start: Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time
- Duration: exactly 48 hours
- Your location: Madrid, Spain (so your local time IS Madrid time)

Calculation:
- Start: October 24, 2026 at 18:00
- Add 48 hours: October 26, 2026 at 18:00

Since you're in Madrid, the end time in your local time is simply 48 hours after the start time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert the contest deadline from PT (Pacific Time) to Madrid time (CET/CEST).

**Given information:**
- Start: October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT
- Submissions close: 72 hours later
- My location: Madrid, Spain

**Calculation:**
- 72 hours after October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT = October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT

**Time zone conversion:**
In late October, Pacific Time is PDT (UTC-7) and Madrid is in CEST (UTC+2) during summer, but by late October, Spain typically switches to CET (UTC+1).

Actually, let me reconsider: In late October 2026, daylight saving time ends in Europe (last Sunday of October is typically October 25, 2026). So Madrid would be in CET (UTC+1).

The US typically ends DST the first Sunday in November, so on October 29, PT would still be PDT (UTC-7).

**Time difference:** UTC+1 (Madrid CET) minus UTC-7 (Pacific PDT) = 8 hours ahead

October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PDT + 8 hours = October 29, 2026 at 6:00 PM CET

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step.

**Submissions close:** October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (Eastern Time)

**Results announcement:** 36 hours later

First, I'll add 36 hours to October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET:
- 11:59 PM ET + 36 hours = November 2, 2026 at 11:59 AM ET

Now I need to convert from ET to Madrid time (CET/CEST):
- In November, Madrid is in CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1
- Eastern Time in late October/early November is EST (Eastern Standard Time), which is UTC-5
- The difference is 6 hours (Madrid is 6 hours ahead)

So: November 2, 2026 at 11:59 AM ET = November 2, 2026 at 5:59 PM CET (Madrid time)

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 17:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert the Unix timestamp 1791788340 to Tokyo time (JST, UTC+9).

First, let me convert this timestamp to a date:
- Unix timestamp 1791788340 represents seconds since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC
- 1791788340 seconds ÷ (86400 seconds/day) ≈ 20,753 days since epoch
- This gives us approximately June 2026

More precisely:
- 1791788340 seconds from Unix epoch
- Converting: This is 2026-06-16 03:59:00 UTC

Tokyo is UTC+9, so I add 9 hours:
- 2026-06-16 03:59:00 UTC + 9 hours = 2026-06-16 12:59:00 JST

ANSWER: 2026-06-16 12:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Calculating Madrid Local Time

The deadline is given in UTC (Z = Zulu time/UTC).

Madrid, Spain is in the **Central European Time (CET)** zone, which is UTC+1 in winter and **Central European Summer Time (CEST)**, which is UTC+2 in summer.

October 25, 2026 falls in autumn, so Madrid will be observing **CEST (UTC+2)** at that time (daylight saving time in Europe typically ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026, but the transition happens at 3:00 AM UTC, after your deadline).

So at 02:30:00 UTC on October 25, 2026, Madrid is still on CEST (UTC+2).

Adding 2 hours: 02:30 + 2:00 = **04:30**

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step.

First, I need to find the last Sunday of October 2026:
- October 2026 ends on October 31st
- October 31, 2026 is a Saturday
- So the last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026

The deadline is 11:59 PM Pacific Time on October 25, 2026.

Now I need to convert Pacific Time to Madrid time (Spain):
- Pacific Time in late October is PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC-7
- Madrid is in CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1 in late October (before the switch to winter time on October 25)
- Actually, let me reconsider: on October 25, 2026, Europe will have already switched to winter time (last Sunday of October), so Madrid would be on CET (UTC+1)
- The time difference is: UTC+1 minus UTC-7 = 8 hours ahead

So 11:59 PM PDT on October 25, 2026 = 07:59 AM CET on October 26, 2026 (next day)

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when the US ends daylight saving time in 2026, convert that to Eastern Time noon, then convert to Lima local time.

In 2026, the US ends daylight saving time on the first Sunday in November, which is **November 1, 2026**.

At 12:00 noon EST (Eastern Standard Time) on November 1, 2026:
- Eastern Time is UTC-5 (standard time, since DST ends at 2 AM that day)
- So 12:00 EST = 17:00 UTC

Lima, Peru is in PET (Peru Time), which is UTC-5 year-round (Peru does not observe daylight saving time).
- 17:00 UTC = 12:00 PET

So the deadline converts to noon in Lima as well.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Converting the Deadline to Tokyo Time

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) means the deadline is set to UTC-12, which is the last timezone on Earth to reach a given date.

**December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE** is equivalent to **January 1, 2027, 00:00 AoE** (midnight starting January 1st in the UTC-12 timezone).

To convert UTC-12 to Japan Standard Time (JST, which is UTC+9):
- UTC-12 to UTC: add 12 hours
- UTC to JST (UTC+9): add 9 hours
- Total offset: 12 + 9 = 21 hours ahead

So January 1, 2027, 00:00 UTC-12 becomes:
- January 1, 2027, 00:00 + 21 hours = **January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST**

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026 to New York time.

**Step 1: Sydney time to UTC**
- Sydney is in AEDT (Australian Eastern Daylight Time) in early October
- AEDT is UTC+11
- 5:00 PM (17:00) on October 5 Sydney time = 6:00 AM UTC on October 5

**Step 2: UTC to New York time**
- New York is in EDT (Eastern Daylight Time) in early October
- EDT is UTC-4
- 6:00 AM UTC on October 5 = 2:00 AM EDT on October 5

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
